articles.text: MĚIGUÓ RÉN: Duìbuqǐ, yìbēi rè kāfēi, zhǐ yào niúnǎi, bú yào táng, yífèn huǒtuǐ sānmíngzhì. Yuè kuài yuè hǎo!
AMERICAN: Excuse me — a cup of hot coffee, with cream only, no sugar, and a ham sandwich. As fast as possible!
XIǍO LIÚ: Měitiān dōu shi "yuè kuài yuè hǎo," nǐ zhēn máng a!
XIǍO LIÚ: Every day it's "as fast as possible." You're so busy!
MĚIGUÓ RÉN: Nǐ zhīdao tāmen gěi wǒ ānpáile nàme duō yào fǎngwènde dìfang. Zhēn shi yìtiān yǒu sānshiliùge zhōngtóu cái hǎo.
AMERICAN: You know, they arranged so many places for me to visit. I only wish that there were thirty-six hours in a day.
XIǍO LIÚ: Hǎo, hǎo. Wǒ mǎshang jiù lái.
XIǍO LIÚ: Okay. I'll be right back.
XIǍO LIÚ: Nǐde sānmíngzhì, kāfēi, niúnǎi.
XIǍO LIÚ: Your sandwich, coffee, and milk.
MĚIGUÓ RÉN: Zhēn kuài. Xièxie ni. Āi, láile sìtiān le, kěshi háishi bù zhīdào zěnme chēnghu nǐ, zhēn duìbuqǐ.
AMERICAN: That was really fast. Thank you. Gee, I've been here four days and I still don't know how to address you. I'm very sorry.
XIǍO LIÚ: Nǐ jiù jiào wǒ Xiǎo Liú hǎo le, bǐjiào róngyi jì.
XIǍO LIÚ: Just call me Xiǎo Liú. It's the easiest to remember.
MĚIGUÓ RÉN: Xiǎo Liú, tīng nǐde kǒuyīn nǐ dàgài shi nánfāng rén. Shi Shànghǎi rén, duì bu duì?
AMERICAN: Xiǎo Liú, your accent sounds like you're probably a southerner. You're from Shànghǎi, right?
XIǍO LIÚ: Nǐ zhēn shi yǔyánxuéjiā, búdàn huì shuō Zhōngguó huà, hái tīngdechū nánfāng, běifāng kǒuyīnde bù tóng.
XIǍO LIÚ: You're a real linguist. Not only can you speak Chinese, you can even tell the difference between a northern and a southern accent.

MĚIGUÓ RÉN: Nǎli, nǎli. Wǒ yánjiūde zhǔyào shi pǔtōnghuà, duì fāngyán méiyou shénme yánjiū, zhǔyào shi wǒ duì Zhōngwén fēicháng yǒu xìngqù. Dōngběi, Xīběi, nánfāng, běifāng, měiyíge dìfang, měiyíge dìqū dōu yǒu zìjǐde yǔyán xíguàn, zhēn shi fēicháng yǒu yìsi.

AMERICAN: Thank you. I mainly do research on Standard Chinese. I'm not well versed in the dialects. The main thing is that I'm very interested in Chinese. Manchuria, the northwest, the south, the north — every place, each district, has its own ways of speech. It's really very interesting.
XIǍO LIÚ: Nǐ duì Zhōngwén zhèiyàng yǒu xìngqù, zhèicì lái fǎngwèn yǒu méiyou gēn Zhōngguóde yǔyánxuéjiā tántan?
XIǍO LIÚ: Since you have such an interest in Chinese, did you talk with some Chinese linguists during this visit?
MĚIGUÓ RÉN: Tán le. Zhèicì Zhōngguó fāngmiàn ānpái wǒ gēn hěn duō xuézhě jiànle miàn. Zhèixiē xuézhě zài guówài dōu shi hěn yǒu míngde.
AMERICAN: Yes. On this trip, the Chinese arranged for me to meet with a lot of scholars who are very famous abroad.
XIǍO LIÚ: Nà hǎojíle. Nǐ kěyi yǒu jīhui duō liǎojiě yìdiǎn Zhōngguó yǔyánxuéde qíngkuàng.
XIǍO LIÚ: That's great. You get the chance to find out more about linguistics in China.
MĚIGUÓ RÉN: Nǐ duì yǔyán yǒu xìngqù ma?
AMERICAN: Are you interested in language?
XIǍO LIÚ: Wǒ? Wǒ duì wénxué, lìshǐ dōu yǒu yìdiǎn xìngqù. Nǐ máng, wǒmen xiàyícì zài tán.
XIǍO LIÚ: Me? I have some interest in literature and history. You're busy — we'll talk some other time.
MĚIGUÓ RÉN: Hǎo, hǎo. Gǎitiān zài liáo. Huí tóu jiàn, Xiǎo Liú.
AMERICAN: Okay. We'll chat some other day. See you later, Xiǎo Liú.
XIǍO LIÚ: Zàijiàn.
XIǍO LIÚ: Good-bye.
